newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds get boost from August durables.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds get boost from August durables.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities performed largely on par with Treasuries after a weaker-than-expected durable goods report boosted both markets.
Most pass-through varieties performed well, but traders mentioned Ginnie Mae and private-label securities specifically.
Ginnie Mae 30-year discount coupons were up 9/32 late on Thursday, about 1/32 higher than most other agency 30-years.
A Ginnie bid list circulated in the afternoon, one trader said. He characterized the seller as a bank.
Overall, agency pass-throughs rose 1/32 to 9/32 by late Thursday afternoon. Thirty-year Freddie Mac 7.5 percents were up 6/32 at 101-7/32, and Fannie Mae 7.5 percents had risen 7/32 to 99-03/32.
Ginnie Mae 7.5 percent coupons were up 6/32 at 99-00/32, yielding 107 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
One trader said private-label pass-throughs saw action. "Conventionals were trading very well ... There was a large buyer," he said.
But another trader described conventionals activity as "two-way."
Fixed-income markets jumped early on Tuesday morning after the Commerce Department said durable goods orders fell 3.5 percent in August, compared with a 3.5 percent rise in July.
"It shows that the signs of strength we were seeing in orders were a mirage," said Tim McGee, chief economist at Tokai Bank Ltd.
